Subject: Deal tethering: node scan and region sizing request

Hi team,

Quick one — DataForge (Soren) has pushed the Q3 commitment forward and wants a firm regional sizing number for APAC (Singapore) plus a fallback in EU for latency-sensitive endpoints. They reiterated that SKU commitments will be tranche-tethered to their usage and that procurement needs a clear SOW line item for node-reserve.

Can we run a short node-scan (approx 48h) on the prospective workload profile Soren shared and return:a) conservative sustained-node recommendation for APAC (12–18 month horizon) b) burst/failover sizing in EU and US c) a pricing delta for dedicated vs. burst lanes (estimate per 1k RPS equivalent).

I've attached their monthly forecast and a short runbook for the scan. Key constraints: 90th pct latency to remain below 150ms for their main route; KV-cache hit expected ~35%; model variant is safemodel-v2-medium (8k context).

Next steps proposed: run node-scan -> compile SLO-shaped capacity chart -> internal OK -> share to procurement. Can Karthik and Ben pick ownership?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deal tethering: node scan and region sizing request

Thanks Neha — happy to take lead on the sizing run. A few clarifying Qs before we schedule the 48h test:

- Can Soren confirm the expected request distribution across routes (ingest / chat / embed)? Even coarse percentages will change batching assumptions.
- Do we run the scan on the quantized-safe model or full FP16 variant? That affects GPU memory and effective concurrency.
- Any hard blackout windows for failover to EU? We need a realistic RTO assumption.

Ben — can you prepare two synthetic load profiles (sustained 3k RPS equivalent and a 10k RPS 30-min burst) based on their forecast so we can map to slot ratios? I can then run the scan in Singapore region (g4/ga-type baseline) and log latency percentiles + KV behaviour.

I'll stand up the run tomorrow morning if we have the answers.

-karthik
Principal Solutions Architect

All,

I've sketched two profiles and attached a brief table in the run notes:

- Profile A (sustained): 3k RPS eq., 45% ingest, 45% chat, 10% embeddings; 8k context avg peek.
- Profile B (burst): 10k RPS eq. for 30 minutes; 60% chat traffic (latency-sensitive).

Notes: with safemodel-v2-medium in quantized mode we get ~18 concurrent streams per A100-equivalent slot; FP16 would drop concurrency by ~25% but improves throughput per-token. For APAC steady-state I'm leaning toward recommending a 6-slot dedicated pool (A100-eq) with a 2-slot burst buffer in shared lanes; EU failover of 4 slots held warm (hot standby) to meet 150ms at 90th for critical chat routes.

I've included estimated hourly burn deltas and a conservative token pricing adj. Attaching run-notes: node-scan-runbook-v1.pdf (subset).

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha / Karthik / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple quick confirmations from our side: 

- Traffic mix: 50% chat, 40% ingest (short summaries), 10% high-dim embeddings.
- Model: safemodel-v2-medium, please test quantized baseline first. If memory looks tight we can evaluate FP16.
- Procurement: they need a clear SOW line for reserved nodes + a separate line for burst buffer when demand spikes.

I'll upload an updated forecast (Q3 ramp) to the Drive link and loop procurement on the SOW draft. No blackout windows — EU failover can trigger instantly but we'd like warm lanes to avoid cold start latency.

Team — great thread. Summary and next steps: 

1) Scan schedule: Karthik to run quantized node-scan in Singapore starting Mon 16 Jun (48h). Ben to validate profiles and capture slot-concurrency metrics.
2) Recommendation (draft): APAC dedicated pool: 6 A100-eq slots reserved; APAC burst buffer: 2 shared slots; EU warm standby: 4 slots (hot-warm) for failover.
3) Commercial: produce two SOW lines — reserved-node monthly rate (6-slot) + burst buffer monthly retainer. Procurement needs explicit failover SLAs and cost for EU warm standby (hot-standby hourly burn).
4) Deliverables: node-scan report + SLO-shaped capacity chart by Wed 18 Jun; draft SOW for procurement by Thu 19 Jun. Neha will own procurement handoff and draft redlines.

Lauren — can you slot time with procurement on Thu to walk the SOW lines? Ben/Karthik — flag any risks to the timeline now.

Neha
